articles.title: Dream Finders 8-K: closes $2.2B Beazer purchase with $572M Millrose land-bank facility
articles.summary: Dream Finders closed its all-cash Beazer purchase Oct. 20, 2026 ($33.50 a share, about $2.2B enterprise value), funded by a $572.1M Millrose land bank facility and $675M of preferred; Millrose says it bought about $488M (net of discount).
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose put land banking and preferred equity behind a top-25 builder merger (homesite count and 12% rate per Millrose's Oct. 27 release), a whole-company financing package Domain will be asked to match.

suggested_update.text: Closed the acquisition of Beazer Homes on 2026-10-20 ($33.50 a share, about $878.4M), funded by $572.1M from a Millrose land bank facility and $675M of 12% Series B convertible preferred, about $488M of it bought by Millrose.

articles.title: Millrose 8-K: Q3 net income $130M, about $9.25B invested capital, $250M buyback
articles.summary: Millrose Q3 2026: net income $130.0M, AFFO $0.80/share, invested capital about $9.25B, $3.4B of it outside Lennar across 21 non-Lennar counterparties; non-Lennar yield 10.8% vs 8.5% on Lennar; $250M buyback authorized.
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose is pricing non-Lennar option capital at about 10.8% and now pairs land banking with preferred equity to win whole-company deals, a benchmark for Domain bids and a package Domain will be asked to match.

suggested_update.text: Millrose closed about $1.1B of capital support on Oct. 20, 2026 for the Beazer acquisition: about $580M of land banking across roughly 7,000 homesites plus about $488M of preferred equity at a 12% dividend.

articles.title: Lennar’s land bank spinoff Millrose bought 1,200 single-family rentals
articles.summary: Millrose bought 1,233 completed Lennar homes in 18 states for about $333M to hold as rentals, disclosed with Q3 results. Hunterbrook, a media outlet whose affiliate is short Lennar and Millrose, had reported the purchases; Lennar stock fell Oct. 2.
articles.why_it_matters: A competitor is taking finished homes off Domain's named customer's books, a service Domain does not offer Lennar, and the short report and lawsuit give Lennar a reason to spread land-bank business to other providers, Domain included.

suggested_update.text: In Q3 2026 Lennar sold 1,233 completed single-family homes in 18 states to Millrose for about $333M, to be held as rentals (per Millrose's Oct. 27, 2026 results release).

articles.title: Lennar snags 444 lots near TSMC’s $265B Phoenix project for $60M
articles.summary: AGWIP Asset Management, described as Lennar's land banker, paid $60.14 million cash for 444 lots on 132 acres near TSMC's north Phoenix site, closing Sept. 15. Seller Aroundtown Agua Fria plans about 2,000 more lots nearby.
articles.why_it_matters: Lennar placed a $60 million Phoenix lot deal with a land banker other than Domain, and the seller has roughly 2,000 more lots coming within three years that will also need land-bank capital; worth confirming whose capital sits behind AGWIP.

suggested_update.text: AGWIP Asset Management, acting as Lennar's land banker, bought 444 lots (132 acres) near TSMC in north Phoenix for $60.14 million cash, closing Sept. 15, 2026 (Phoenix Business Journal via KTAR).

articles.title: Starwood Capital Group and Trez Capital Announce Strategic Partnership Focused on U.S. Residential Land Financing
articles.summary: Starwood Capital and Canada's Trez Capital announced Nov. 3, 2026 a partnership to originate land acquisition and development loans for US single-family communities, seeded with a $450M Trez loan portfolio and targeting more than $1B of originations a year.
articles.why_it_matters: Starwood is putting institutional capital behind A&D loans at $1B-plus a year, a debt alternative builders and developers can use instead of a Domain land bank; Anthony Murphy at Starwood and John Hutchinson at Trez lead it.

articles.title: Strata Land launches as builders face land-capital squeeze
articles.summary: Strata Land Partners launched Nov. 2, 2026, backed by Wafra and Hunt Companies and led by Michael Forsum, former Landsea Homes president. Its first projects cover about 1,300 lots; capital committed was not disclosed.
articles.why_it_matters: A new land-capital platform aimed at public and especially private builders nationwide, run by an operator who knows builders personally, is a direct new competitor for Domain's mid-size builder deals.

articles.title: Millrose Properties, Inc. Announces Pricing of $1.0 Billion Senior Notes Offering
articles.summary: Millrose priced $1.0B of senior notes Sept. 22 and closed Oct. 6, 2026: $500M 6.500% due 2029 and $500M 6.750% due 2031. Proceeds and a $500M term-loan draw may buy Dream Finders–Beazer homesites and repay an $850M revolver balance.
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose raised about $1.5B of fresh debt partly to take on Dream Finders–Beazer homesites; its 6.5%–6.75% unsecured cost of funds is a benchmark for how cheaply Domain's main rival can price option deals.

suggested_update.text: Millrose priced $1.0B of senior notes on Sept 22, 2026, partly to acquire homesites from the combined Dream Finders–Beazer; the 2031 tranche must be redeemed if the deal had not closed by May 13, 2027.

articles.title: Five Point Holdings, LLC Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
articles.summary: Five Point Q3 2026: revenue $14.6M, net loss $4.4M, no land sales closed, deferred to 2027; full-year net income guide about $20M; liquidity $576.2M. Hearthstone land banking: about $3.4B under management ($2.8B fee-paying), $6.5M quarterly fees ($18.2M year to date).
articles.why_it_matters: Five Point owns rival land banker Hearthstone, backed by Blue Owl-managed funds, so this sizes a competitor at about $3.4B under management and shows California land sellers deferring sales rather than cutting prices.

articles.title: Texas County and District Retirement System commits $200m to TPG Essential Housing IV
articles.summary: Texas County and District Retirement System committed $200M to TPG Essential Housing IV, a TPG Angelo Gordon closed-end fund seeking $3B of equity; Kern County's pension committed $50M in August.
articles.why_it_matters: TPG Angelo Gordon is raising a $3B fourth Essential Housing fund and pensions are writing $200M tickets, which means more competing land-bank capital chasing the same builders and the same LPs Domain courts.

articles.title: AREC raises $390 million to finance lot and land deals for builders
articles.summary: Avila Real Estate Capital raised $390M from an insurer and a university endowment, taking total capital above $750M. It lends against land, lots and homes for builders; investors include D.R. Horton, LGI, Century, Toll, Dream Finders and DRB.
articles.why_it_matters: A builder-backed lot lender with a stated goal of financing 100,000 lots in five years is competing capital for the finished-lot deals Domain funds, and six top-20 builders are its investors.

articles.title: Millrose 8-K: amends Lennar founder's rights and Kennedy Lewis management agreements
articles.summary: On Aug. 27, 2026 Millrose amended its Founder's Rights Agreement with Lennar (Priority Amount for Lennar's capital priority right; its secured-financing collateral consent right) and its Kennedy Lewis management agreement (investment guidelines scope, reimbursable expenses). No figures disclosed.
articles.why_it_matters: Changes to Lennar's priority claim on Millrose capital and to what Kennedy Lewis is allowed to invest in determine how much Millrose capacity is free to compete for Domain's other builders; the exhibits are worth reading.

suggested_update.text: On Aug. 27, 2026 Lennar and Millrose amended the Founder's Rights Agreement, adjusting the Priority Amount for Lennar's capital priority right and its secured-financing collateral consent right (amounts not stated in the 8-K body).

articles.title: Arixa Capital Surpasses $9 Billion in Loan Originations, Expands Homebuilder Finance Program
articles.summary: Arixa Capital passed $9 billion in loan originations and is expanding homebuilder finance under new EVP Jim Sawitzke, ex-Brio Homebuilder Solutions (Blackstone). Its Pro Builder program recently made $30M to $80M loans in seven states.
articles.why_it_matters: Another private lender is scaling acquisition-through-construction loans of up to $80 million to established builders, a substitute for land-bank capital, and Sawitzke is a contact worth knowing.

articles.title: Century Communities Triples Dallas-Fort Worth Footprint with Acquisition of HistoryMaker Homes
articles.summary: Century Communities bought substantially all assets of HistoryMaker Homes (HMH Lifestyles), a Dallas-Fort Worth builder founded in 1949, closing Oct. 7, 2026; price undisclosed. It roughly triples Century's DFW community count, adding 29 communities, in one Grapevine division.
articles.why_it_matters: The 10th-largest builder absorbed the 77th, consolidating DFW lot positions; any option or land-bank contracts HistoryMaker held now sit with Century, so Domain should check its exposure and approach Century's DFW land team.

suggested_update.text: Acquired substantially all assets of HistoryMaker Homes (DFW) on Oct 7, 2026 (price undisclosed), tripling its Dallas-Fort Worth community count.

articles.title: KB Home 8-K: real estate EVP Albert Praw to retire Nov 30, no successor named
articles.summary: KB Home's Albert Z. Praw, EVP Real Estate and Business Development, will retire November 30, 2026 after more than 30 years. He is expected to advise on land relationships and transactions for up to a year; no successor named.
articles.why_it_matters: KB Home's top land executive is leaving with no successor named, so whoever takes over land decisions at the seventh-largest builder is a person Domain should identify and call now, while Praw is still advising on land relationships.

suggested_update.text: Albert Z. Praw retires as EVP, Real Estate and Business Development effective November 30, 2026 (8-K filed November 16, 2026); he stays as a non-employee adviser on land relationships for up to one year and no successor has been named.

articles.title: Century Communities 8-K: Jim Francescon named President from Jan 1; Robert stays CEO
articles.summary: Century Communities' board on Nov. 4, 2026 elected James (Jim) Francescon, 37, EVP of corporate operations, President effective Jan. 1, 2027, overseeing homebuilding, land and M&A. Robert Francescon stays CEO and sole principal executive officer; Dale Francescon stays Executive Chairman.
articles.why_it_matters: The next-generation leader at a top-10 builder is now named, and he comes from private equity and investment banking, so he is a person Domain should get in front of on land-capital decisions.

suggested_update.text: James Francescon (EVP, Corporate Operations) becomes President effective 2027-01-01; Robert J. Francescon remains CEO and becomes sole principal executive officer (8-K filed 2026-11-09).

articles.title: DAVID WEEKLEY HOMES NAMES NEW CFO AND ADDS CMO TO LEADERSHIP TEAM
articles.summary: David Weekley Homes named Adam Zylman CFO on Aug. 31, 2026, succeeding Heather Humphrey, who retires after 33 years and stays as an adviser. Zylman founded Grey Owl Partners and co-founded Sunland Capital.
articles.why_it_matters: David Weekley, the 17th-largest builder, has a new CFO from private equity. He now decides how it funds land, so Domain should introduce itself.

suggested_update.text: Adam Zylman named CFO (announced 2026-08-31), succeeding retiring CFO Heather Humphrey, who moves to an advisory role.

articles.title: S&P downgrades Dream Finders to ’B+’ following $2.2B acquisition of Beazer Homes
articles.summary: S&P cut Dream Finders to B+ from BB- (stable outlook) after it closed the $2.2B all-cash Beazer acquisition, citing about $720M of assumed Beazer notes and debt-like preferred; it cites $800M of land-bank capital from Millrose.
articles.why_it_matters: A single-B Dream Finders with leverage expected to stay elevated through 2028 needs off-balance-sheet lot capital more than ever, and the article names Millrose as its land-bank partner with $800M, so Domain is competing against Millrose for the combined company's lots.

suggested_update.text: Oct 20, 2026: S&P downgraded Dream Finders to B+ from BB- (stable) after closing the $2.2B Beazer acquisition; report cites $800M of Millrose land-bank capital.

articles.title: Lennar 424B5: prices $600M of senior notes due 2029 and 2032
articles.summary: Lennar priced $600M of senior notes Oct. 13, 2026 and closed them Oct. 15: $300M 5.700% due 2029 (T+80) and $300M 5.950% due 2032 (T+95), expected ratings Baa2/BBB/BBB+. Net proceeds about $594.5M for general corporate purposes.
articles.why_it_matters: Lennar, a named Domain relationship, can still borrow unsecured for three to five years at under 6%, which is the cost of capital any land-bank proposal to it is measured against.

suggested_update.text: Priced $600M of senior notes on 2026-10-13: $300M 5.700% due October 2029 and $300M 5.950% due January 2032, net proceeds about $594.5M for general corporate purposes.

articles.title: Lennar 8-K: Q3 net earnings $284M on $8.0B revenue; delivery guide cut to 80,000-81,000
articles.summary: Lennar Q3 (Aug 31): net earnings $284M ($1.19/share) on $8.0B revenue; deliveries 20,840, orders down 9%, gross margin 15.8%. Controls about 488,000 homesites, under 2.5% owned; called rising option maintenance fees a real cost. Delivery guide cut to 80,000-81,000.
articles.why_it_matters: Lennar is almost fully land-light with $7.33B of deposits and pre-acquisition costs outstanding, so its lower delivery guide and thinner margin bear directly on takedown pace and option pricing for its land bankers, Domain included.

suggested_update.text: At Aug 31, 2026 Lennar owned or controlled about 488,000 homesites with under 2.5% owned; homebuilding debt to total capital 16.6%; fiscal 2026 delivery guide lowered to 80,000-81,000 homes.

articles.title: Housing M&A shifts as global capital retargets residential futures
articles.summary: At the Zelman Housing Summit, Essential Housing CEO Steve Benson said land banking costs builders about 200-250 bp over blended capital cost and that the firm, with over $22B originated in five years, is raising about $10B more.
articles.why_it_matters: A direct competitor publicly stated its pricing (200–250 bp over builders' blended cost) and a roughly $10B capital raise, which tells Domain how a rival is pitching builders and how much capacity is coming.

suggested_update.text: At the Oct 2026 Zelman summit, Stanley Martin (Daiwa House) set a 10,000-closing target for 2027, said three recent acquisitions including Holiday Builders add about $1B of revenue, and is pausing single-family acquisitions to integrate them.

articles.title: Lennar 8-K: restates revolver at $3.795B, main tranche extended to Nov 2031
articles.summary: Lennar on Oct. 26, 2026 restated its unsecured revolver: commitments rise to $3.795B with a $750M accordion, and the main tranche extends to November 2031. It also drew $40M more term loan, to $1.75B due May 2028.
articles.why_it_matters: Lennar has locked in more and longer bank liquidity at slightly lower cost, which sets the bank-debt benchmark Domain's land-bank pricing to Lennar is measured against.

suggested_update.text: Revolving credit facility amended and restated 2026-10-26: commitments $3.795B plus $750M accordion, Class A maturity November 2031; term loan increased to $1.75B, due May 2028.

articles.title: LGI Homes 8-K: amends revolver to about $1.166B, $855M extended to Oct 2030
articles.summary: LGI Homes amended its revolver on Oct. 9, 2026: commitments about $1.166B (down from $1.1825B), $855M extended to Oct. 9, 2030, and an accordion of up to $175M (up from $95M) capped at $1.3B. Wells Fargo is agent.
articles.why_it_matters: LGI just reset the bank line that funds its land, a natural moment to ask whether it wants off-balance-sheet lot capital alongside it.

suggested_update.text: Revolver amended 2026-10-09: commitments about $1.166B (down from $1.1825B), $855M now maturing 2030-10-09, accordion up to $175M (up from $95M) capped at $1.3B total; Wells Fargo agent.

articles.title: Dream Finders 8-K: accordion adds $220M, revolver commitments to about $1.7B
articles.summary: Dream Finders Homes exercised a committed accordion on Oct. 9, 2026, raising its revolving credit commitments by $220M to about $1.7B. Other terms unchanged.
articles.why_it_matters: Dream Finders was stacking bank capacity days before closing Beazer, alongside Millrose's land bank and preferred, showing how much outside capital this customer now needs.

suggested_update.text: Revolving credit facility commitments increased by $220M to about $1.7B via accordion exercise on 2026-10-09.

articles.title: Century Communities 8-K: credit facility raised to $1.2B, extended to Nov 2030
articles.summary: Century Communities amended its credit agreement on Sept. 30, 2026: commitments rise to $1.2B and maturity extends to Nov. 1, 2030 for extending lenders. Flagstar and Morgan Stanley join; BMO does not extend. U.S. Bank is agent.
articles.why_it_matters: Century has a larger, longer bank revolver to fund land on balance sheet, which reduces its near-term need for land-bank capital.

suggested_update.text: Credit agreement amended 2026-09-30: aggregate commitments increased to $1.2B and maturity extended to 2030-11-01 for extending lenders.

articles.title: Dream Finders 8-K: Q3 1,967 closings, net income $6.7M after $23M Beazer deal costs
articles.summary: Dream Finders Q3 2026: 1,967 closings; net income $6.7M after $23M of Beazer deal costs. Beazer acquisition closed Oct. 20, all cash, about $2.2B enterprise value. Controlled lots 52,574; lot deposits $490.2M; net debt-to-capital 48.1%.
articles.why_it_matters: Dream Finders now carries Beazer at 48.1% net leverage and says it expects Q4 abandonment charges from terminating land deals that miss return thresholds, so its lot-option counterparties face walk-aways while the combined builder needs off-balance-sheet land capital.

suggested_update.text: Completed the all-cash acquisition of Beazer Homes on Oct. 20, 2026 at an enterprise value of about $2.2B; controlled lots were 52,574 and lot deposits $490.2M at Sept. 30, 2026.

articles.title: Forestar 8-K: chairman Tomnitz retires; CEO Anthony Oxley adds executive chairman role
articles.summary: Forestar executive chairman Donald J. Tomnitz retired effective Oct. 31, 2026; CEO Anthony W. Oxley added the executive chairman role Nov. 1 as D.R. Horton's designee. Stacey H. Dwyer joined the board. Tomnitz advises through Sept. 2028.
articles.why_it_matters: Forestar is D.R. Horton's majority-owned lot developer and an alternative to third-party land banking for the largest builder, so Oxley now holding both top roles is the person who sets how much of Horton's lot supply stays in-house.

suggested_update.text: At Forestar (D.R. Horton's majority-owned lot developer), Donald J. Tomnitz retired as Executive Chairman effective Oct. 31, 2026 and President/CEO Anthony W. Oxley became Executive Chairman as well on Nov. 1, 2026.

articles.title: HHHunt names CFO Ann Kelly as next CEO in 2027 C-suite reset
articles.summary: HHHunt will make CFO Ann Kelly CEO on July 1, 2027; CEO Buck Hunt stays chairman. SVP of finance and treasury Steve Brant becomes CFO; COO Steve Fritz stays.
articles.why_it_matters: HHHunt's finance chief is moving up and its treasurer is taking the CFO seat, so the people who would sign a land-bank deal there are changing and worth a call.

suggested_update.text: CFO Ann Kelly becomes CEO July 1, 2027 and SVP finance and treasury Steve Brant becomes CFO; Buck Hunt remains chairman (announced Oct 2026).

articles.title: Century Communities 8-K: Q3 2,442 deliveries, EPS $0.44, full-year guidance lowered
articles.summary: Century Q3 2026: 2,442 deliveries, EPS $0.44; full-year guidance lowered. Revolver upsized to $1.2B, extended to November 2030. Lots 60,969, 45.1% controlled; finished lot costs fell 3% sequentially. Record 343 communities; 360-370 expected at year-end including 29 from HistoryMaker.
articles.why_it_matters: Century's net leverage rose to 34.9% from 25.9% at year-end as it drew on its revolver and bought HistoryMaker, which makes it a builder with a reason to move more lots off balance sheet and one Domain should call (the revolver upsizing itself is scored on its own 8-K).

suggested_update.text: Acquired substantially all assets of HistoryMaker Homes on Oct. 7, 2026 (Dallas active communities from 12 to 41) and at the end of Q3 2026 upsized its revolver to $1.2B with maturity extended to November 2030.

articles.title: Lennar Financial Health, Subsidiary Spin-Off Draw Investor Suit
articles.summary: A Lennar shareholder filed a proposed securities class action in the Southern District of Florida against Lennar and two executives, alleging misleading statements about financial health and a subsidiary spinoff, including capitalized land-bank option costs.
articles.why_it_matters: The suit puts Lennar's accounting for land-bank option costs, and by extension the 2025 Millrose spin-off, under litigation scrutiny. That could change how Lennar and other builders structure and disclose option deals with Domain.

articles.title: Meritage 8-K: Q3 closings down 14% to 3,187, EPS $1.04; 31% of lots optioned
articles.summary: Meritage Q3 2026: 3,187 closings, down 14%; EPS $1.04; no Q4 guidance. Land spend $329M versus $528M. Of about 71,800 lots, 69% owned and 31% optioned, against a roughly 40% off-balance-sheet target. Net debt-to-capital 18.9%; revolver undrawn.
articles.why_it_matters: Meritage owns 69% of its lots against a 40% off-balance-sheet target while cutting land spend, so the fifth-largest builder has room to move lots into option structures; worth a call to its land and finance team.

articles.title: Forestar 8-K: FY2026 13,545 lots sold, $1.64B revenue; FY2027 guide 12,000-13,000 lots
articles.summary: Forestar fiscal 2026 (to Sept. 30): 13,545 lots sold, revenue $1.64B, net income $142.6M; Q4 average lot price $108,300. Owns 58,200 lots, controls 26,200; liquidity $1.3B. Fiscal 2027 guide: 12,000-13,000 lots, $1.4B-$1.5B revenue.
articles.why_it_matters: Forestar is the main finished-lot alternative to a land bank and is guiding to fewer lot deliveries next year, a read on builder takedown demand and on how much D.R. Horton lot supply it will cover.

articles.title: D.R. Horton 8-K: FY2026 84,202 closings, $33.0B revenue; 77% of 570,600 lots controlled
articles.summary: D.R. Horton fiscal 2026: 84,202 closings, $33.0B revenue, EPS $10.11. Lots 570,600, 23% owned and 77% controlled. Repaid $600M of 1.3% notes in October; bought back $3.6B of stock. FY2027 guide: 79,000 to 84,000 closings.
articles.why_it_matters: The largest builder moved to 77% controlled lots with 68% of closings on Forestar or third-party-developed lots, while total lots fell to 570,600 and guidance is flat to down, so its demand for new third-party lot capital is steady rather than growing.

suggested_update.text: At Sept. 30, 2026 D.R. Horton held 570,600 lots, 23% owned and 77% controlled (down from 591,900 a year earlier), and it repaid $600M of 1.3% senior notes at maturity in October 2026.

articles.title: KB Home 8-K: Q3 revenue down 20% to $1.30B, net income $65.3M; $722M land spend
articles.summary: KB Home Q3 (Aug 31): revenue $1.30B, down 20%; net income $65.3M; 61,581 lots, about 60% owned and 40% under contract; debt to capital 35.7%; $415M drawn on revolver; land spend $722M, up 40%.
articles.why_it_matters: KB Home still owns about 60% of its lots while leverage climbs and it borrows on its revolver to fund land, which is the profile of a builder that could use land-bank capital.

suggested_update.text: At Aug 31, 2026: 61,581 lots (about 60% owned, 40% under contract), debt to capital 35.7%, $415.0M drawn on the credit facility, total liquidity $942.4M.

articles.title: Smith Douglas 8-K: Q3 831 closings, net income $3.0M; gross margin 16.3% vs 21.0%
articles.summary: Smith Douglas Q3 2026: 831 closings, $262.5M home closing revenue, net income $3.0M; closing gross margin 16.3% versus 21.0% a year earlier. Controls 24,724 lots, about 92% optioned. Debt to book capitalization 18.8%, up from 9.0% at year-end.
articles.why_it_matters: Smith Douglas runs almost entirely on optioned lots, so a five-point margin drop and doubling leverage tell Domain how much room this kind of customer has left to pay option costs.

suggested_update.text: At Sept 30, 2026: 24,724 controlled lots, 22,693 optioned (about 92%); notes payable $101.4M; debt to book capitalization 18.8% (9.0% at Dec 31, 2025).

articles.title: LGI Homes 8-K: Q3 closings up 11.6% to 1,189, EPS $1.05; 2026 guide 4,600-4,800
articles.summary: LGI Homes Q3 2026: 1,189 closings, up 11.6%; EPS $1.05. Lots 58,400 (50,270 owned, 8,130 controlled). Net debt-to-capital 40.6%; liquidity $447.7M. 2026 closings guide narrowed to 4,600-4,800; targets 180-plus communities by end-2027 from 151, partly via developers' finished lots.
articles.why_it_matters: LGI still owns 86% of its lots at 40.6% net leverage and calls its position predominantly self-developed and on balance sheet, which makes it one of the larger untapped candidates for a land-bank conversation.

articles.title: LGI Homes, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
articles.summary: LGI Homes reported Q3 2026: net orders fell 61.2% to 609 and backlog to 685 homes. It owned 50,270 lots and controlled 8,130 at Sept 30; net debt-to-capital was 40.6% and liquidity $447.7M.
articles.why_it_matters: LGI owns most of its lots while orders collapse and its controlled count grows, so it is a candidate for land-light capital Domain could offer.

suggested_update.text: At Sept 30, 2026: 50,270 owned and 8,130 controlled lots, net debt-to-capital 40.6%, liquidity $447.7M (Q3 2026 results, Nov 3, 2026).

articles.title: NVR 8-K: Q3 settlements down 7% to 5,268, EPS $89.45; lots controlled up to 185,300
articles.summary: NVR Q3 2026: 5,268 settlements, down 7%; EPS $89.45; gross margin 18.3% versus 21.0%. Lots controlled rose to 185,300 from 175,300. About $24.8M of contract land deposit impairments. Repurchased $237.2M of stock.
articles.why_it_matters: NVR, the pure lot-option builder, wrote off about $24.8M of lot deposits in one quarter while still adding 10,000 controlled lots, a sign that option deals struck at earlier prices are being walked or reserved against.

articles.title: Downtown Las Vegas land sells for big new housing project
articles.summary: Nevada sold the roughly 23-acre former Grant Sawyer state office site in downtown Las Vegas for $10.6 million to a New York investment firm, which reportedly gave Lennar an option for a 1,000-plus-home project (snippet only; paywalled).
articles.why_it_matters: If the paywalled report holds, an unnamed New York investor is land-banking a Lennar site, so Domain should find out which firm is taking Lennar option deals in Las Vegas; scored from the snippet only.

suggested_update.text: Reported 2026-11-15: a New York investment firm bought the former Grant Sawyer site in downtown Las Vegas for $10.6 million and gave Lennar an option on it for a planned 1,000-plus-home project.

articles.title: IHP Capital Partners acquires 1,458 acres in Brazoria County, Texas, for new residential community
articles.summary: IHP Capital Partners, with developer Scarborough Lane Development, agreed to buy 1,458 acres in Brazoria County, Texas, for the Peachtree master plan (about 3,400 finished lots). A first phase of 206 acres and 535 lots has closed; price not disclosed.
articles.why_it_matters: A rival residential land capital provider is committing to a multi-phase, roughly 3,400-lot Houston-area position, finished lots that builders there could buy instead of using a Domain land bank.

articles.title: M/I Homes 8-K: Q3 2,241 deliveries, EPS $2.56; 52% of 48,934 lots under contract
articles.summary: M/I Homes Q3 2026: 2,241 deliveries, down 2%; EPS $2.56. Lots 48,934, about 48% owned and 52% under contract. Q3 land spend $135.2M on purchases plus $154.4M on development. Homebuilding debt-to-capital 18%; undrawn $900M facility; $50M of buybacks.
articles.why_it_matters: M/I already has 25,509 lots under contract and keeps buying land with $620M of cash and an undrawn revolver, so it can self-fund and would use Domain only if the option cost beats very cheap balance-sheet capital.

articles.title: Why 2027 may turn into a land negotiation year for homebuilders
articles.summary: Scott Cox of SLC Advisors expects 2027 to bring land re-trades and real price cuts, with builders refusing roughly 10% land-bank carry and pushing slower takedowns. He predicts Millrose will cut option fees and ease takedowns to keep assets.
articles.why_it_matters: An opinion piece, but it is the argument builders' land teams will bring to Domain in 2027: lower option fees, softer takedowns, and a claim that Millrose's asset-based fee makes it concede first.

articles.title: Why homebuilders and lot sellers no longer price risk the same way
articles.summary: Tony Avila (Builder Advisor Group, Avila Real Estate Capital) says patient-capital lot sellers can hold out while builders underwrite at lower margins; bank AD&C lending is ~$90B vs $200B+ in 2006, with private land capital filling the gap.
articles.why_it_matters: Describes a widening gap between lot-seller pricing and builder underwriting and names a private debt fund (AREC, backed by ~15 builders) competing to fund lots, which bears on Domain's option pricing and competing capital.

articles.title: Millrose Properties: New Builder Capital Earns 210 Basis Points More

articles.why_it_matters: Shows the roughly two-point premium Millrose charges builders other than Lennar, a reference point for Domain's own option pricing.

articles.title: Tri Pointe 8-K: Q3 1,084 deliveries, $706.8M revenue; $21.1M inventory charges

articles.why_it_matters: Tri Pointe's release refers to its integration into the Sumitomo Forestry Group, so land-financing decisions on its 15,761 controlled lots may now be shaped by a parent with its own capital rather than by third-party land bankers.

articles.title: Taylor Morrison Home stock ends after USD 6.8 billion deal
articles.summary: Berkshire Hathaway closed its Taylor Morrison purchase July 24, 2026 at $72.50 a share (about $6.8B equity, $8.5B enterprise value), pairing it with Clayton Properties; it now calls itself the fourth-largest US builder and holds over 10% of Lennar.
articles.why_it_matters: Berkshire now owns a top-10 builder through Taylor Morrison and Clayton and holds over 10% of Lennar, a deep-pocketed owner that can fund land on balance sheet rather than through land bankers like Domain; the deal closed before the window, so no M&A floor.

articles.title: Japanese-owned builders are cutting U.S. outlooks: what’s next?

articles.why_it_matters: The Japanese owners of Stanley Martin, DRB and Tri Pointe are pivoting from acquisitions to capital efficiency, including less capital tied up in land, which could raise their demand for off-balance-sheet lot structures.
